doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

title: Hearing the great saxophone sections
summary: He recalls the sections of Carter, Ellington and Basie, and liking Buddy Tate more than Lester Young at the time.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So you saw some of the great saxophone sections coming through there.

Yes, yes. Benny Carter had a — oh my goodness, he had a lead alto player named Porter Kilbourn who was almost as ferocious as he himself was. And of course the great Duke Ellington had Johnny Hodges and Otto Hardwick and Harry Carney. And of course the Basie saxophone section with Earle Warren, Tab Smith, Don Byas, or Buddy Tate and Lester Young.
So you got to hear Lester in the Basie band?
Yes. And believe it or not, I liked Buddy Tate more at the time.
He was a very strong kind of Texas tenor sound, right?
Yes. A big old strong Texas tenor, yeah.
